Public Health Center 28, Krung Thonburi Road

This was my first time here, for dental treatment. I couldn't get it done yet because I only recovered from COVID two weeks ago. I need to be fully recovered for a month before I can have dental work done. So I made a new appointment. I needed teeth cleaning and fillings, but the staff informed me that only one procedure can be done at a time.

If you need dental treatment, you need to arrive early in the morning to get a queue number. Arrive no later than 7:00 AM because they only issue 10 queue numbers per day. The service process is:
1. Get a queue number.
2. Wait to be contacted by staff downstairs before going up to the second floor.
3. Present your queue number at the registration counter.
4. Weigh yourself, measure your height and proportions, have your temperature and blood pressure checked.
5. Wait to be called to your examination room.
6. Enter the examination room.

Overall, the staff provided good service.
I've been there twice. The staff were very polite, from the queueing area downstairs to the doctor. They provided service with a heart... Thank you to the valuable staff of this organization.

This was my first visit. The doctors, nurses, and all the staff provided excellent and convenient service.

Public Health Center 28, Krung Thonburi
Conveniently accessible via BTS, Krung Thonburi station.

The service is excellent, but only for Burmese. A Thai person went at 7 a.m. and by 2 p.m., they were still waiting aimlessly. They should put a sign at the entrance of the center saying "Services provided for Burmese only." There's 1 Thai person for every 30 Burmese people. There are very few Thai patients. I called, but no one answered. I made an appointment for us to call to ask about the test results. I called exactly at the appointment time, but no one answered on both lines... I will stand in mourning for the rest of my life. 😤😱💀
